_comment: One file per row, named <row id>.json — `verify.py <row_id>` reads exactly this name, and
there must be ONE OF THESE PER ROW in outcome-rows.jsonl. A row with no file scores a hard
0.0000, which is indistinguishable from a catastrophically bad arm; an orphan file here means
a row was renamed and something is now silently ungraded. `/coder-eval:task` step 6 checks
both directions before a stage is paid for.
REPLACE every marker below. This file is core-1's; its three siblings are core-2.json,
regression-1.json and regression-2.json.
`path` is the artifact, resolved against the SANDBOX (the grader's cwd at run time).
`checks` maps a check to its params. The key is a name from verify.py's CHECKS table,
optionally suffixed with #<label> so one check can be declared several times — four
`mentions#...` checks below rather than one with four needles, because each check is pass
or fail and the score is passed/applicable: a row with ONE check can only score 0.0 or 1.0,
which is the zero-variance shape an outcome suite exists to avoid. Several independent
checks are what make the row continuous. FOUR APPLICABLE CHECKS IS THE FLOOR: below that a
row's score takes at most five values and behaves like a binary grader.
A name with no entry in CHECKS is SKIPPED and excluded from the denominator, so a typo here
cannot inflate a row — but it cannot fail one either, which is why the discrimination gate
grades a known-good artifact and expects 1.0.
`json_field` below declares no `field`, which is how a check opts OUT of a row when the same
expectations are templated across rows: it returns NOT APPLICABLE and leaves the numerator
and the denominator. Note what makes that legal — the trigger is this FILE declaring nothing,
never the artifact being the wrong shape. See verify.py's docstring: an N/A that keys on the
artifact lets an arm shrink its own denominator by ignoring a requirement.
Prove the whole set discriminates before spending on a stage: `/coder-eval:task` step 6.5.
